title: Mitigate cross-tenant GPU OOM surge via epochal KV snapshot and slab compaction backoff
creator: Aisha Reynolds
description: Summary: Several production incidents (hosted + dedicated pools) over the last 48 hours resulted in sudden multi-tenant GPU OOM waves and degraded tail-latency. Symptoms: bursty 90-99th percentile latency, rapid increase in per-GPU resident memory, and asymmetric slab starvation on nodes running mixed-length chat sessions. Root cause (triage): a combination of (1) aggressive slab compaction heuristics interacting poorly with epochal KV snapshot writes causing transient KV index amplification, and (2) a corner-case where prefix KV tombstones from high-throughput sessions bypassed the usual batching window and turned into many small allocations, fragmenting the tensor arena. This pushed several nodes past soft OOM thresholds and caused host-level eviction storms. Fix implemented: backport and extend a compact-backoff heuristic and introduce an epochal KV snapshot coalescer that collapses concurrent tombstone writes into single journal entries; limit instantaneous compaction concurrency to 1 per-GPU when per-node free memory < 18%. The runtime patch is minimal: a 28-line change to the compactor scheduling logic, new KV-coalescer stage, and an additional guard in the allocator that defers large prefix allocations until compaction quiesces. Impact: reduces transient allocation spikes and avoids micro-allocation cascades that previously caused GPU OOMs during high-concurrency workloads. Repro steps: 1) Start 120 concurrent sessions with mixed short/long prompt distributions and a steady prefix-update client that deletes then re-inserts keys at 50 ops/sec. 2) Limit node RAM to a medium bucket profile (simulate Hosted-dense). 3) Observe slab fragmentation and small-allocation churn after ~6–12 minutes. Patch repo/PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7234 (internal). Canary / rollout: staged canary on 4 dedicated nodes in us-west-2 (mixed pools) -> monitor memory headroom and OOM count for 2 hours -> expand to remaining dedicated nodes -> finally merge to hosted fleet with gradual ramp. Rollback: revert change-set and re-enable previous compactor concurrency flags; keep extra monitoring retention for 24h. Monitoring: dashboard panels created: GPU OOMs per-host, slab-free-fragments, allocator-small-alloc-rate, KV-journal-write-rate. Alert thresholds: OOM > 1 in 30m on canary nodes triggers immediate rollback. Communications: customers affected notified in private support threads; incident summary posted to #incidents and to affected CS contacts.

postmortem_summary: The incident resulted from a timing interaction between compaction scheduling and high-frequency prefix tombstone writes. The system lacked a coalescing path for concurrent tombstone writes, which amplified index churn and produced many tiny allocations that fragmented the allocator. The runtime patch reduces compaction concurrency under low-memory pressure and coalesces epochal tombstones into single writes. Immediate customer impact was mitigated by throttles and the hotfix; long-term actions recommended below.
